answer: Autonomous agents managing cargo along a wharf mitigate Sybil attacks via ultra-wideband ranging against a stationary radio beacon. By validating nanosecond signal propagation delays relative to an anchor near a monitored relic, the network binds each cryptographic key to a discrete physical location. An adversary incurs the verifiable cost of powering separate radio transceivers per forged identity. However, multipath reflections can distort pulse timing and trigger false rejections.
